usageNotes: Permanently removes a single entry (identified by its zero-based order index) from an SDN route map. The route map must exist and the caller must hold SDN.Allocate on the route-map path; after deletion, apply the SDN configuration to push the change cluster-wide. If the global SDN config is currently locked by another operation, pass the matching lock-token to avoid a conflict error.

examples.summary: Delete the first entry (order 0) from a route map named 'rm-transit'

destructiveReason: Permanently deletes the specified route map entry; any BGP policy rule that relied on this entry will stop matching after the next SDN apply.
tips: Entry order indices are not automatically renumbered after deletion — verify remaining entries' orders before referencing them in subsequent calls.
Changes take effect cluster-wide only after calling the SDN apply endpoint; deletion alone does not update the running FRR/BGP configuration.
Retrieve the current entry list first (GET on the entries collection) to confirm the correct order index before deleting.
